name: Siemens
summary: Siemens documents distinct CONNECT 400/Drivetrain Analyzer, PLC-based SM 1281, and Senseye routes. The archived SAM GUARD attribution is wrong: Precognize/SAM GUARD belongs to SAMSON Group.

flows.name: SIMOTICS CONNECT 400 motor monitoring

steps.label: CONNECT 400
steps.detail: Motor-mounted module measures vibration, temperature and magnetic field.

steps.label: Wi-Fi / HTTPS
steps.detail: Module transmits measurements over Wi-Fi to Drivetrain Analyzer Cloud using encrypted HTTPS.

steps.label: Drivetrain Analyzer Cloud
steps.detail: The Insights Hub application analyzes drive-train operation and condition.

steps.label: Cloud asset view
steps.detail: Users view motor status, analysis and maintenance guidance in Drivetrain Analyzer Cloud.

flows.caveat: The documented destination is Drivetrain Analyzer Cloud, not automatically Senseye or a generic SIDRIVE IQ Fleet layer.

flows.name: SIPLUS CMS1200 / SM 1281 PLC monitoring

steps.label: Vibration probes
steps.detail: Sensors supply vibration signals to the SM 1281 condition-monitoring module.

steps.label: S7-1200 backplane
steps.detail: SM 1281 is integrated with SIMATIC S7-1200 and configured in TIA Portal.

steps.label: SM 1281 module
steps.detail: Module performs vibration monitoring; library blocks expose status and recording controls to the PLC.

steps.label: PLC / HMI
steps.detail: The control program can use module status and traffic-light information for local presentation.

flows.caveat: This is an automation-module route; the cited source does not make cloud upload or Senseye a required next hop.

flows.name: Senseye predictive maintenance

steps.label: Existing machine data
steps.detail: Condition indicators and context can come from existing sensors or historians.

steps.label: Senseye ingestion
steps.detail: Supported routes include API, MQTT, email, object storage or direct historian connection.

steps.label: Senseye insights
steps.detail: Analytics assess measures; an Attention Index scores the asset's need for review.

steps.label: Cases
steps.detail: A medium or high Attention Index opens a case with supporting insights for maintenance review.

flows.caveat: Senseye is a separate cloud application that can use existing data; no required CONNECT 400 or SM 1281 feed is documented.

findings.archived_claim: vendor-product-catalogue.md §5: CONNECT 400 uses Wi-Fi and reports into Siemens motor-monitoring software.
findings.assessment: The Siemens manual confirms Wi-Fi / HTTPS transmission into the Insights Hub application Drivetrain Analyzer Cloud.

findings.archived_claim: vendor-product-catalogue.md §5: SM 1281 is an S7-1200/TIA Portal condition-monitoring module.
findings.assessment: Siemens' application example shows SM 1281 in S7-1200 and its TIA Portal library, including status and raw-data functions.

findings.archived_claim: vendor-product-catalogue.md §5: Senseye uses an Attention Index for case prioritization.
findings.assessment: Siemens' developer documentation says the index is an ML-based score and medium/high levels create cases with evidence.

findings.archived_claim: vendor-product-catalogue.md §5 and vendor-landscape-eight-majors.md: SAMguard (ex-Precognize) listed as Siemens.
findings.assessment: SAMSON says it acquired Visual Process/Precognize in 2018 and offers SAM GUARD. Its own material identifies Precognize as a SAMSON company; SAM GUARD should not be mapped as Siemens.

findings.archived_claim: vendor-product-catalogue.md §5: Senseye Attention Index = anomaly probability × degradation rate × asset criticality, with automated RUL.
findings.assessment: Siemens confirms an ML-based Attention Index and cases, but the reviewed developer pages do not publish that formula or establish RUL as an obligatory stage in this flow.

unknowns: An automatic integration between CONNECT 400/Drivetrain Analyzer Cloud, SM 1281 and Senseye is not established by the reviewed official sources.
Senseye's proprietary scoring model and hosting internals are not disclosed in the cited developer documentation.
